parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the C-C-C bond angle and the hybridisation shown by the carbon atoms in benzene.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Benzene reacts with chloroethane in the presence of a catalyst. The reaction mechanism is called electrophilic substitution.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
The first step in the reaction is the generation of the $^{+}\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ electrophile.

Write an equation for the reaction that generates this electrophile.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Describe the mechanism for the reaction between benzene and the $^{+}\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ electrophile. Include all relevant curly arrows and charges.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Chlorobenzene and chloroethane have different reactivities in nucleophilic substitution reactions.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Identify a suitable reagent to illustrate this difference in reactivity.

The reagent chosen should give **visibly** different results with chlorobenzene and chloroethane.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Write equations to describe any reactions that occur.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Explain the difference in the reactivities of chlorobenzene and chloroethane in nucleophilic substitution reactions.
